common_name: Diamond Delight Euphorbia (Compact Mounding Baby's Breath Euphorbia)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Diamond Delight is a more compact, tightly mounding selection than Diamond Frost, suited to smaller containers and tighter spacing in beds.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, and avoid overwatering, since this euphorbia tolerates dry conditions far better than soggy soil. Diamond Delight is a compact, densely mounding euphorbia selection covered almost continuously in tiny, airy white flowers that create a soft, baby's-breath-like haze over fine-textured foliage, providing months of low-maintenance filler color from spring through frost without deadheading. Its smaller, tighter habit compared to the taller, more billowing Diamond Frost makes it especially useful in mixed containers and small beds where a lower, more restrained mound is wanted, while still delivering the same nonstop bloom and heat tolerance that made the Diamond series popular. As with other euphorbias, the milky sap can irritate skin and eyes, so use gloves when pruning or handling cut stems.
sources: Proven Winners — Diamond series euphorbia notes

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; EnduraScape was bred specifically for improved resistance to powdery mildew, the disease that most commonly ends the season early for older verbena cultivars in humid Gulf South summers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun, and avoid overhead watering where possible, since good air circulation further reduces the already-low mildew risk on this series. EnduraScape is a landscape verbena series bred for outstanding heat and humidity tolerance combined with strong resistance to powdery mildew, the fungal disease that commonly disfigures and shortens the bloom season of older verbena cultivars in the hot, humid Gulf South. It forms a dense, fast-spreading, low mat covered in clusters of small flowers continuously from spring through frost, holding up to summer heat with minimal fading or dieback compared to less disease-resistant verbena types. Its vigorous, weed-suppressing spread and low-maintenance disease resistance make it well suited to mass plantings, slopes, and hot, sunny beds where reliable, long-season color is the priority.
sources: Proven Winners and Darwin Perennials — EnduraScape verbena series notes

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in moist, rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Redhead is a sun coleus selection bred to hold its brilliant color and resist fading or scorching in full Gulf South sun, unlike older shade-only coleus cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, and water regularly, since the large, colorful leaves wilt more readily than average bedding plants in dry conditions. Redhead is a sun-tolerant coleus selection prized for its intensely saturated, solid red-orange, deeply serrated foliage that holds its vivid color from spring through frost without fading, even in the intense light of a full-sun Gulf South garden where many older shade-bred coleus scorch. Its bold, fiery color makes a striking contrast planted alongside chartreuse, silver, or deep purple companions in a mixed bed or large container. Pinch flower spikes as they form to redirect the plant's energy into leaf production rather than seed, and pinch growing tips periodically through the season to encourage a fuller, bushier shape.
sources: Proven Winners — ColorBlaze coleus series notes

common_name: Under the Sea Coleus (Uniquely Lobed Fringed-Leaf Coleus Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Under the Sea selections tolerate more sun than traditional shade coleus but still benefit from afternoon shade protection in the hottest Gulf South locations.

directions: Plant in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, and keep soil consistently moist to support the lush, textural foliage this series is grown for. Under the Sea is a distinctive coleus series bred for unusual, deeply lobed, ruffled, or fringed leaf shapes that resemble coral, anemones, or seaweed, giving each named selection within the series a strikingly different silhouette and texture from typical broad-leaved coleus, in a range of colors from deep burgundy to chartreuse and coral-pink. The novel foliage forms make the series a favorite for adding textural contrast and conversation-piece interest to shaded containers, fairy gardens, and mixed beds alongside broader-leaved companions like hosta and heuchera. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant's energy in leaf production, and pinch growing tips periodically for a fuller, bushier habit through the season.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company — Under the Sea coleus series notes

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Suncredible produces a large number of full-sized flowers on a well-branched, taller plant, blooming continuously without the deadheading a traditional single-stem sunflower requires.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun after the last frost, and expect a taller, more upright, heavily branching habit than compact landscape sunflower series. Suncredible is a vegetatively propagated sunflower bred for continuous rebloom, producing full-sized, classic golden sunflower blooms with dark centers in huge numbers from a single well-branched plant over a long summer-to-frost season, without the need to deadhead or replant as is required with traditional single-bloom seed sunflowers. Its taller stature and heavier bloom load make it a strong choice for the middle or back of a sunny border, a cutting garden, or a large container where its abundant flowers can be enjoyed both in the garden and as cut flowers. Stake in windy sites if needed, and feed regularly through the season to sustain its extended, heavy bloom production.
sources: Simply Beautiful Gardens — Suncredible sunflower series notes
